name: Apple Silicon Mac, 256 GB unified (M3 Ultra class)
gpu: up to 80-core integrated GPU, shares the 256 GB unified pool
notes: The 256 GB tier is what separates this from mac-128gb: enough unified memory to hold large MoE builds (and long-context KV) that a 128 GB Mac cannot.
Bandwidth is the reason it exists for inference: M3 Ultra's 819 GB/s is ~3x a MacBook-class M4 Max (546 GB/s) and ~3x an M4 Pro, so decode scales with it. M2 Ultra is 800 GB/s.
M3 Ultra configs are 96/128/256/512 GB; this class covers the 256 GB tier reported on. Apple later discontinued some capacity tiers — a setup should state the exact config.
Runtime is MLX / llama.cpp-Metal (and oMLX-style wrappers); no CUDA, so CUDA-only speculative forks do not apply.
Memory pressure is configurable (sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb); the default GPU wired limit is well below 256 GB.

identity.name: Apple Mac, M3 Ultra / M2 Ultra, 256 GB unified

memory.note: per-chip bandwidth: M3 Ultra 819 GB/s, M2 Ultra 800 GB/s (each on its variant); CPU and GPU share one pool.

compute.cpu_cores: M3 Ultra: up to 32 (24 performance + 8 efficiency)
compute.note: M3 Ultra: 32-core Neural Engine, up to 80-core GPU. Apple publishes Neural Engine core counts but no GPU FLOPS, so TFLOPS stay null.

thermal.note: Apple does not publish chip TDP.

sources.note: Mac Studio (2025) tech specs: M3 Ultra 32-core CPU / 80-core GPU / 32-core Neural Engine, 819 GB/s memory bandwidth, up to 512 GB unified memory
M3 Ultra: up to 80-core GPU, 32-core Neural Engine, over 800 GB/s memory bandwidth, unified memory configurable up to 512 GB
